Each player commands a team of geckos, navigating a dynamically evolving garden made of hex tiles, forming patterns and bug chains to score victory points. The game blends tactical tile placement with the excitement of collecting bug meeples, strategically achieving secret and communal objectives along the way. As the garden grows and geckos scamper, players must balance resource management and strategic foresight to emerge as the master of this charming, bug-filled realm. Replenish 4 Special Actions 5 Game End & Scoring Game Overview As nimble geckos, we compete in a lush garden for the finest bounty of insects. We navigate through a dynamically evolving terrain to form bug chains and occupy specific patterns. By tactically placing garden tiles and skillfully positioning our geckos, we secure valuable prey and fulfill communal and secret objectives. Goal of the Game Collect the most victory points by capturing bugs and completing objective cards (bug chains or terrain patterns). Gameplay A turn always consists of four fixed steps: 1. Expand the Garden Choose one of your 3 hand tiles and place it adjacent to the existing garden. Patterns on the edges must match perfectly. 2. Position Geckos Place one of your 5 geckos on the edge between the tile just played and an adjacent tile. The gecko must bridge two identical terrain patterns. If all of your geckos are already in the garden, you may instead move an existing gecko to the new position. 3. Claim Objectives Check if you meet the requirements of one of the 6 face-up objective cards (Bug Objectives or Terrain Objectives). You may only claim an objective if you actively contributed to its completion during this turn by placing a tile or moving a gecko. 4. Replenish Draw a new tile from the stack to refill your hand to 3 tiles. Special Actions Action Description Capture Bugs If a tile is completely surrounded by other tiles, the player with the majority of adjacent geckos receives the corresponding bug meeple. In case of a tie, the active player wins. Adaptation Once per turn, you may spend a previously captured bug meeple to exchange your entire hand for 3 new tiles. Game End & Scoring The game ends after the current round once a player achieves their 6th objective, a bug supply is exhausted, or the last tile has been drawn. Scoring is calculated as follows: Each completed objective card is worth 1 point. Each collected bug meeple is worth 1 point. Each bug on the bottom of a completed objective is worth 1 point. Additional points are awarded for your fulfilled secret objective (either for specific bug types or the largest continuous terrain pattern). [Rating: 5/10] Very tactical, at least with three players - I can't imagine playing with more would be any fun at all. As it was I had no opportunities to affect my private scoring card and not a lot of interesting decisions in other areas. Probably better with two.

[Rating: 5/10] [b][url=https://boardgamegeek.com/video/554073/garden-geckos/garden-geckos-review-15-minutes-can-save-you-15-pe]Dice Tower Reviews: Garden Geckos [/url][/b]

[Rating: 5/10] A serious design flaw holds my score back. If you want me to constantly look for/at diamond shapes than put up a dotted outline on the tile. It was maddening for me to flick my eyes back and forth from the state of the board to the objective cards to see my geckos positioning. The gameplay is Ok but there are so many better tile-layers in this this category. A+ for components.

[Rating: 5/10] Tile laying mixed with contract fulfillment. Overall, the game is serviceable but it is pretty busy to look at. Figuring out what land tiles and insects you're connected it with is a chore. My eyes are constantly going back and forth for a game that's not complicated at all. The random draw of tiles and goal cards can be frustrating at times, too. The gameplay works but I'm not all that excited to play it, would prefer other options in this genre.

[Rating: 6/10] Tile and geckos placement to earn majorities on tiles and complete objectives. It is cute idea, but gameplay is very abstracted.

[Rating: 6.5/10] This is a fun little tile laying game about geckos in a garden that are trying to capture and eat? different bugs. The gameplay is super simple but the scoring can be a bit AP inducing as the board grows bigger over the course of the game.
